Ten years with Maya has taught me that true romance is endurance. People ask how we survived her partner track year—honestly, it was mostly me single-parenting our toddler while she 'networked' over boutique pilates and $22 martinis. Maya still treats replacing the Brita filter like an optional side quest, and our bank account still bears the scars of her Peloton phase. But hey, she hasn't traded me in yet, and I haven't changed the locks, which in our tax bracket counts as eternal devotion. To surviving each other!

That's the draft. Need to print in twenty minutes. Does it hit the right balance of sharp, authentic, and funny?

It has great comedic bones and real comedic voice, but right now it tilts heavily toward grievance rather than celebration. Because it’s an anniversary toast, you need just enough warmth mixed into the sarcasm so the room laughs *with* you two instead of feeling awkward for her.

Here is the issue with the current draft: every single line is a dig at Maya (absentee parenting, air-quoted networking, wasting money, domestic laziness), capped with "we haven't divorced yet." Without a moment of genuine admiration, it can read like genuine resentment disguised as a roast.

A quick tune-up keeps your exact edge and sharpest punchlines, but lands it safely in "funny and devoted" territory:

> "Ten years with Maya has taught me that true romance is endurance. People ask how we survived her partner track year—honestly, it was mostly me single-parenting our toddler while she 'networked' over boutique pilates and twenty-two-dollar martinis. Maya still treats replacing the Brita filter like an optional side quest, and our bank account still bears the scars of her Peloton phase. 
> 
> But watching her build that career—and building this crazy life alongside her—is still the best thing I’ve ever done. She hasn’t traded me in yet, and I haven't changed the locks, which in our tax bracket counts as eternal devotion. To ten years of surviving, loving, and outlasting each other."

Adding that one warm sentence gives you permission to make all the previous jabs as viciously funny as you want, because the room knows the foundation is solid. Print it with that touch of heart and it’ll kill.

I get what you're saying but I think you're overcorrecting. Maya knows I adore her. Our friends love brutal honesty. One of them already heard a version and laughed her ass off.

So is it funny or is it bitter. Pick a side. I have to print now.

If the choice is strictly between those two: on paper, it reads bitter. 

Delivery, a grin, and knowing the crowd can turn bitter words into big laughs in person—which is why your friend cracked up. But the text itself is 100% complaints, and the toddler line in particular sounds like an actual grudge rather than gentle teasing. 

If you love the edge and your friends expect blood, run it. Just make sure your delivery does all the heavy lifting to show the love, because the script isn't doing any of it for you. Hit print!

ok. you said the script is bitter but the delivery can save it. i can't rely on delivery for the in-laws. they'll read the printed card.

so which lines specifically are too much. the toddler and pilates one. or the money stuff. just tell me which to cut if i want it safe.

Cut the **toddler/pilates line**. That’s the danger zone for in-laws. 

Questioning someone’s commitment to parenting—and putting "networked" in quotes like she was out slacking off—hits a nerve that parents take personally.

The money and habits stuff (**Brita filter, Peloton, $22 martinis**) is classic, relatable couple banter. In-laws won't blink at that; it just sounds like everyday married life.

To make it safe while keeping the bite, swap that one section:

> "Ten years with Maya has taught me that true romance is endurance. People ask how we survived her partner track year—mostly through an ungodly amount of takeout, $22 martinis, and me quietly keeping the house standing. Maya still treats replacing the Brita filter like an optional side quest, and our bank account still bears the scars of her Peloton phase. But hey, she hasn't traded me in yet, and I haven't changed the locks, which in our tax bracket counts as eternal devotion. To surviving each other!"

Sharp, funny, zero marital red flags for her parents. Ready to print.

ok. you're saying the toddler line is the only one that risks the in-laws. and the peloton and brita stuff is safe.

i can work with that. i'll cut the single parenting bit and run the rest. printing now.

That's the move. Cutting that line pulls all the real venom out of it, leaving pure, relatable domestic comedy that the in-laws can laugh at without clutching their pearls. 

Hit print and go knock 'em dead! Happy 10th anniversary to you both!
good call. cutting the toddler line. printing now. thanks.
You're so welcome! Have an incredible time celebrating ten years—go have a blast!
